intro.text: The Control Tower sees every request that enters the city's web servers. Screens blink with URLs.
Quack. Flask is a Python framework. A route ties a URL to a function, and the function returns the page.

mid.text: Requests flow. Now trace which function answers which, and keep user input out of dangerous places.
Quack. Careful with user input: it is where most web bugs start.

outro.text: Requests routed, queries safe. The tower runs the whole city's traffic.
Quack. Last stop: the Oracle, where an AI tries to answer everything.

games.title: Route Board
games.instructions: Use the server code to answer.

rounds.explain: The path is /search. The part after ? is the query string, not the route.

rounds.q: In search(), where does the value of q come from?
rounds.explain: request.args holds query-string parameters. A POST form body is in request.form.

rounds.q: A form uses method="post" to /login. What must the route allow?
rounds.explain: Routes default to GET only. List POST in methods to accept form submissions.

rounds.q: Which is the safe way to run SQL with a user's input?
options: db.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?", name)
db.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = " + name)
Strip spaces from name and concatenate it
rounds.explain: Placeholders keep user text as data, so it can't change the query. Building the string by hand invites SQL injection.

rounds.q: What does {{ name }} do in a Jinja template?
options: Prints the value of the variable name into the page
rounds.explain: Double braces insert a value. Jinja also escapes it by default.
